title: Terraform module for managed GPU node groups and hybrid autoscaling (ASG & Karpenter) in Private deployments
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that provisions GPU-backed node groups inside customer VPCs for Redwood Private deployments. The module must support two autoscaling backends: EC2 Auto Scaling Groups (ASG) for predictable capacity reservations and Karpenter for fast, bin-packing-style scaling. The module must be configurable to work with both our on-prem packaging and cloud VPC variants, handle GPU AMI selection, attach GPU drivers via DaemonSet, expose health-checking hooks, and provide upgrade-safe lifecycle hooks for kernel/driver updates. This ticket covers module implementation, unit/integration tests, CI checks, and a rollout plan with canary and rollback strategies.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exports documented variables and outputs and can be consumed by the private deployment repo without local modifications
Module supports two autoscaling modes: 'asg' and 'karpenter' via a single boolean/mode flag
GPU node groups are provisioned with correct instance types, labels, taints and nodeSelector-compatible tags for Redwood workloads
GPU driver installation is automated using a DaemonSet and module exposes a helm chart / manifest path override
Health checks report node-level GPU readiness (nvidia-smi probe), kubelet status, and instance reachability to Redwood monitoring
Upgrade flow documented and tested: rolling kernel/driver upgrades without losing KV cache more than 5% of requests during a canary
Integration test runs in CI that provisions ephemeral VPC + nodes with ASG and with Karpenter, validates scheduling of a GPU workload, and tears down cleanly
Module includes IAM policies scoped to minimum privileges for node join, spot/interrupt handling, and Karpenter controller if enabled
Security review checklist completed and security_review_required flagged if any cloud provider privileges are elevated
Documentation and example usage added to private-deployments/infra and a sample stack in staging is created
tasks: Design module interface (variables/outputs) and share in design doc
Implement Terraform module: compute resources, node group autoscaling options, IAM roles, autoscaling policies
Add support for GPU AMI lookup and bootstrap userdata that registers node with Redwood agent
Create Karpenter provisioning template examples and ASG launch templates with GPU flags
Implement DaemonSet for NVIDIA drivers with node affinity to GPU nodes and preflight readiness probe
Add health-check metrics (prometheus exporter + logbeat) and new dashboards in Console
Write CI integration tests that spin up ephemeral infra in a dedicated staging account
Run upgrade/rollback tests and document steps for operators
Create example consumption module in private-deployments/stacks/staging-gpu.tf
Open PRs for module and private-deployments integration, request security review
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Ticket created. Initial scoping meeting with Platform and IR team. Decided to support hybrid mode (both ASG and Karpenter) behind a single 'autoscaler_mode' variable.
2025-02-21: Prototype of TF module skeleton committed to feature/gpu-nodegroups. Basic variables and outputs added. Linked initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1823

2025-02-24: POC validated that Karpenter can provision GPU instances with our provisioning template; noticed bootstrap userdata timeout on some instance types — added retry logic to agent join script.
2025-02-27: Security raised concern about IAM permissions for spot interruption lifecycle hooks. Added scoped policies and documented justification in design doc.

2025-03-03: Integration tests added to CI pipeline but failing intermittently on AWS spot reclaim behavior. Investigating backoff and node termination handling. Updated test matrix to include non-spot runs for determinism.
decisions: Use unified 'autoscaler_mode' variable with allowed values ['asg','karpenter'] to simplify module API
Default to 'asg' for enterprise customers who require reserved capacity; enable 'karpenter' for bursty workloads in cloud deployments
Install GPU drivers via DaemonSet instead of AMI bake to simplify upstream AMI management and enable rolling driver upgrades
Expose an 'upgrade_hook' variable to allow custom pre-drain and post-drain commands for KV cache persistence
Require security review if module is configured with broad account-level permissions or cross-account roles
